A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ImViD research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The shorter v2 retains the supplementary content through repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction benchmarks, a 21-expert sound-field study in Table 5, and a 58-participant sound-field ablation study in Figure 11.

after.justification: v2 retains the original reconstruction benchmarks and both sound-field user studies, including their numerical and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The capture procedure, STG++ affine color mapping, and training-free sound-field reconstruction pipeline remain unchanged, including the implementation described in Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the seven-scene ImViD collection and the same reconstruction evaluation coverage: Scenes 1, 2, 5, and 6 across the main text and appendix. No task or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: The evaluated 4DGS, 4Drotor, and STG comparators remain unchanged. The Ex4DGS comparison in Appendix C.1 and Figure 10, and the sound-field ablation variants, already appear in v1.

E3.justification: Both retain the same 300-frame evaluation, segmentation rules, cam10 test view, A100 training setup, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, and user-study designs and participant counts.

E4.justification: The temporal color-continuity analysis, baseline failure analyses, direction/distance ablations in Figure 11, and noise-reduction comparison in Figure 12 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same descriptive percentages and average user ratings. Neither adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The benchmark and user-study results match throughout. For example, STG++ retains Opera test PSNR 31.240, and Figure 11 retains full-model direction/distance scores of 3.91/3.07. Qualitative findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 and their assumptions are unchanged, including the single omnidirectional sound source and distance-scaled room response. Appendix D's color-transform equation moves between pages without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the immersive audiovisual dataset, moving capture rig, reconstruction benchmark, and multimodal 6-DoF VR pipeline.

C2.justification: The baseline mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged, including difficult motion, residual local flickering, and expensive moving-rig calibration. Appendix reflow does not add or remove qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix A changes the demo's stated availability from a future release on an under-construction homepage to 'You can see a video demo on our homepage.' No homepage address is added; implementation and reproducibility details otherwise match.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2, Appendix B, and Tables 1 and 8 are unchanged. Changed bibliography back-reference page numbers reflect repagination.

P1.justification: Appendix A's demo notice is shortened, and the acknowledgment changes an NSFC grant number from 62171255 to 62422110. The remaining narrative, terminology, and section order are retained.

P2.justification: Appendix text and equations reflow around retained figures. Section E.5 moves onto the preceding page, eliminating its mostly empty standalone page; Tables 6–8 and Figure 13 shift forward. Figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The funding update, revised demo notice, and appendix reflow are small maintenance edits. Methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, and limitations remain identical. The demo notice adds no access address, so these changes do not establish a meaningful overall improvement in clarity, scientific support, or reproducibility.
